name: Eldgjá fissure eruption
summary: A VEI-6 basaltic fissure eruption at Eldgjá in southern Iceland, the largest effusive eruption of the past 1,500 years, releases ~219 megatonnes of SO₂. Chronicle reports of darkened skies and cold winters across Europe and the Mediterranean coincide with the eruption window.

_quarry.structural_significance: Documented climatic forcing event coinciding with reported famine and political crisis in mid-10th-century Europe; appears to have prompted Christianisation pressure on still-pagan Iceland.
